pick.name: Vercel Pro (Next.js hosting)
pick.what: Managed hosting made by the Next.js team: previews, edge network, AI Gateway integration
pick.why: Best Next.js experience; $20 per developer seat/month with $20 usage credit, 10M CDN requests, 1TB transfer; Hobby is personal non-commercial only
pick.free_limits: Hobby: free, 1 seat, personal non-commercial use only

best_free.name: Cloudflare Workers (Next.js via adapter)
best_free.what: Edge hosting: Free plan 100,000 requests/day, 10ms CPU per invocation; Paid from $5/month
best_free.why: Cheapest scalable host; Next.js runs via OpenNext adapter
best_free.free_limits: Free: 100,000 requests/day, 10ms CPU per invocation; Paid from $5/month (10M requests, 30M CPU-ms included). Free use is not limited to non-commercial purposes; Free Services may not process card data on the web property.

alts.name: Netlify
alts.free_limits: Free: 300 credits/month (production deploy 15 credits, bandwidth 20 credits/GB); commercial use on Free not stated

alts.name: Coolify (self-hosted PaaS on a VPS)
alts.why: Lowest running cost and no lock-in; you own the ops
alts.maintained: release date not shown on repo page (opened 2026-10-28)

candidates.name: Render / Railway / Fly.io
candidates.verdict: Not evaluated; good for long-running backends

decision: Vercel Pro is the best overall host for a Next.js product (previews, zero-config, AI Gateway) at $20/seat/month, and Hobby cannot be used commercially. Cloudflare Workers is the best low-cost or free route and suits Hono APIs; self-host when ops skill exists and bills matter.
note: Same answer as the Ship track: Vercel Pro when you want every Next.js feature with no adapter, Cloudflare Workers through OpenNext when you need a free plan that allows commercial use. Vercel's Hobby plan is non-commercial.
details: Netlify and Coolify evaluated from their pricing/repo pages.

verify.note: Checked against primary sources; wording made neutral during verification.
